overall_summary: Deduplicated performance analysis indicates that space-related topics—specifically extreme planetary conditions, extreme astrophysical objects, and 'What If' hypothetical space scenarios—are massively outperforming other niches in views-per-day and engagement metrics (likes/comments-per-view). Videos published within the last 7 days (e.g., Venus having a longer day than year, falling into liquid diamond planets, and the dark planet TrES-2b) are driving the highest velocity, while psychology, everyday science facts, and old animal comparisons are lagging in comparison.

winning_patterns.evidence: Videos like 'What If You Fell Into a Liquid Diamond Planet?' (1,024 views in < 10 days) and 'Venus Has a Day Longer Than Its Year' (968 views in ~2 days) show exceptional short-term velocity.
winning_patterns.action: Produce more hypothetical planetary entry or bizarre astronomical rule videos using high-contrast visual hooks in the first 2 seconds.

winning_patterns.pattern: Extreme Material / Odd Weather in Space
winning_patterns.evidence: 'The Planet Darker Than Coal: TrES-2b' (1,026 views) and 'This Planet Rains Supersonic Rubies!' (721 views) maintain strong continuous traction.
winning_patterns.action: Focus on bizarre meteorological phenomena on distant exoplanets (e.g., glass, rubies, liquid metal) paired with cinematic motion graphics.

weak_patterns.pattern: Abstract Psychological Tricks / Brain Hiding Facts
weak_patterns.evidence: Titles like 'Your Brain Can Create Fake Memories' (5-53 views) and 'The Psychological Trick to Stop Songs Stuck in Your Head' (71 views) suffer from low velocity and weak engagement.
weak_patterns.action: Deprioritize standalone psychological advice shorts unless tied to a shocking, counter-intuitive neurological anomaly or true-crime behavioral micro-mystery.

weak_patterns.evidence: Older animal facts like 'Octopuses Have THREE Hearts' or 'The Only Animal That Can Live Forever' show flatlining view counts and minimal repeat interaction over the 7-day observation window.
weak_patterns.action: Pivot animal-related content away from simple trivia toward cinematic animal survival, high-stakes predator-prey micro-narratives, or prehistoric paleontology mysteries.

next_video.concept: What Happens If You Step Foot on the Rogue Planet Flying Through Deep Space Without a Star?
next_video.opening_direction: Start in absolute pitch-blackness with zero ambient light, followed by the sudden realization of absolute freezing temperatures dropping instantly.
next_video.twist_direction: Reveal that despite being millions of miles from any sun, the core is boiling hot due to radioactive decay, creating a hidden subterranean ocean underneath miles of ice.
next_video.reason: Capitalizes on the winning 'What If' and extreme dark planet traction (similar to TrES-2b and liquid diamond planet successes) while introducing a completely fresh astronomical phenomenon (rogue planets).
fresh_topic_constraints: Do not use black holes, diamonds, rain materials, or sharks.
Must explore rogue planets / interstellar wanderers.
Keep pacing under 21 seconds with high visual contrast.

experiment: Test a 21-second 'What If' space scenario with a zero-light hook vs. a text-on-screen curiosity hook to measure 3-second drop-off rates and audience retention.
